title: Home Battery Rebates in Sacramento 2026: SMUD Pays $300 per kWh | HomePowerRebate
desc: SMUD's My Energy Optimizer Partner+ pays $300 per kWh up to $6,000 for a home battery, down from $500 and $10,000 on September 23. Eligible brands, rules and steps.
lead: SMUD cut its home battery incentive on September 23, 2026, from $500 per kilowatt-hour to $300, with the household cap falling from $10,000 to $6,000. If your project was submitted for interconnection by September 22, the higher amount may still apply.
cards_intro: These figures come from SMUD's battery storage page, which we read on October 2, 2026. The incentive is a one-time enrollment payment for joining My Energy Optimizer Partner+, and you must be on SMUD's Solar and Storage Rate.

cards.title: New amount, from Sept 23, 2026
cards.note: Up to $6,000 per household, for interconnection applications received on or after September 23.

cards.title: Earlier amount
cards.note: Up to $10,000 per household, only if the project was submitted for interconnection by September 22 and enrolled by December 31, 2026.

cards.title: Quarterly incentives
cards.note: Ongoing quarterly incentives are available for Tesla batteries at present. Other makers get the enrollment incentive only.

cards.title: Enroll within
cards.note: Of receiving permission to operate (PTO) from SMUD.

after_cards:
What that means in dollars

A 13.5 kWh battery earns 13.5 x $300 = $4,050 at the new rate, and 13.5 x $500 = $6,750 under the old one. The new cap of $6,000 is reached at 20 kWh. SMUD says it will always leave 20% of the battery in reserve at the end of an event in case of an overnight outage.
sections: SMUD excludes individual rental units until it can find a way for owners and tenants to share the benefit, and multifamily homes follow the same tenant restriction. Customers on the MED rate are not eligible, and neither are income-qualified customers whose battery, solar or equipment costs SMUD covers fully, though they can still join the program. You also need a battery installed at the home and enrollment in the Solar and Storage Rate. Check each of these before you sign a contract.

Joining means SMUD can use some of your battery's capacity at times when demand is highest, which could include shifting when the battery powers your home. SMUD says participants keep full access to the power in the battery during an outage and describes the interactions as seamless. The program's terms and conditions have the details, and they are worth reading before you commit.
Eligible brands and the interconnection fee

SMUD lists Eguana, Enphase, Franklin, SolarEdge, Sonnen and Tesla as eligible. If you add a new solar system with a battery, or a battery only, there is a one-time interconnection fee. If you add a battery to an existing solar system, there is none. Your installer should know about the fee, and you should ask for it in the quote.

SMUD serves Sacramento and sets its own solar and storage rules, which differ from those of the investor-owned utilities. Questions go to SaveEnergy@smud.org, and SMUD says it replies within two business days. Sacramento averages about 5.1 peak sun hours a day (2020 to 2024), so a battery paired with solar has good sun to store. SMUD pays no cash rebate for solar panels that we found; the battery incentive is where its money goes.
The federal 25C and 25D tax credits ended after December 31, 2025. That makes SMUD's enrollment incentive more important for anyone planning a battery in 2026.
claim_heading: How to claim the SMUD battery incentive
claim_steps: Confirm that SMUD is your electric utility and that you are not on the MED rate or in an individual rental unit.
Choose a battery from an eligible maker: Eguana, Enphase, Franklin, SolarEdge, Sonnen or Tesla.
Ask your installer when the interconnection application will be submitted, since the date decides the rate.
Join SMUD's Solar and Storage Rate.
After SMUD gives permission to operate, enroll in My Energy Optimizer Partner+ within 90 days.
faq: How much does SMUD pay for a home battery?

$300 per kWh up to $6,000 per household for interconnection applications from September 23, 2026. Earlier projects submitted by September 22 and enrolled by December 31, 2026 can still get $500 per kWh up to $10,000.
Eguana, Enphase, Franklin, SolarEdge, Sonnen and Tesla.
Not individual rental units, according to SMUD. Multifamily homes follow the same tenant restriction.
Do I need a special rate?
Yes. You must participate in SMUD's Solar and Storage Rate and enroll in the program within 90 days of permission to operate.
Is there a SMUD solar panel rebate?
We found no SMUD cash rebate for solar panels. Its battery enrollment incentive is the main incentive.
